name: commitwork
description: Repository security scanner, local CI runner and scheduled monitor, with remediation and compliance-evidence tooling. Manifest-driven; runs against any git repository.
filesNote: The publishable unit is the whole tracked tree except the export-ignored paths in .gitattributes: ci/, CLAUDE.md, docs/TRAPS.md and monitor/data/advisory-cvss.json. This list is the npm package's subset: the runtime directories, mcp/ (the MCP server, and mcp/tools.mjs, which the wire layer licenses under Apache-2.0), and the licence files the package's licence statements point to. LICENSE-APACHE-2.0 is listed because npm's automatic inclusion takes LICENSE but not a suffixed name, so without the entry the Apache carve-out ships without its text; bin/test/npm-pack-contents.test.mjs holds the list to the wire-layer manifest. Without a files list npm packs the working tree minus ignore rules, including CLAUDE.md, ci/, docsite/ and any untracked local file: npm pack reads the WORKING TREE, so an untracked local file ships while a gitignored one does not. LICENSING.md is listed because `license` says SEE LICENSE IN LICENSING.md and npm's automatic inclusions cover LICENSE/LICENCE, not this filename, so omitting it leaves the licence field pointing at nothing. With a files list npm does not read the root .gitignore, so a gitignored file inside a listed directory ships whenever it is on disk. The release packs a clean checkout, where none exists; the negations mirror each .gitignore rule that covers a listed directory so a local pack leaves them out too, and the same test plants one file per rule to keep the two lists in step.
